title: VPC Hardware Hedging Matrix and Runway Workbook
body:
Overview:
This workbook is a pragmatic, zone-level capacity planning sheet designed for Private/VPC customers that need a hedged hardware purchase strategy. It prioritizes short-term runway (0–12 months), mid-term tranches (12–30 months), and spare rotation rules to reduce single-point supply risk.

Why this is different: instead of a single BOM sizer this file encodes a hedging matrix — mix GPUs across three procurement tranches, target a spare-rotation window (in months) per zone, and compute GPU-equivalent safety stock for heterogeneous fleets (A100-80GB equivalent). The output is a recommended tranche-by-zone purchase schedule with cost bands and utilization sensitivity.

Assumptions (editable parameters):
- Target P50 sustained throughput (tokens/sec) per zone: 1,200k
- Target P90 sustained throughput per zone: 2,000k
- Typical model mix: 60% chat-heavy (long context), 30% batching-friendly, 10% offline/rerank
- Typical sequence length distribution median: 384 tokens, 95th: 1024 tokens
- Baseline GPU types and their A100-80GB-equivalent factors:
  * A100-80GB: 1.0
  * H100-80GB: 0.72 (higher perf -> lower equivalent factor for capacity counting)
  * L40s: 1.15 (lower memory, higher footprint for long-context)
  * RTX-6000: 1.9 (treat as fallback burst units)
- Expected effective utilization target (P50): 65% (goal), P90 headroom target: 40%
- Spare-rotation window target: 6 months (means we keep enough spare GPUs to replace failures and allow 6 months of scheduled rotation without backorder)
- Procurement lead times: 6–12 weeks (domestic), 12–24 weeks (global special orders)

Key metrics computed (sheet columns):
- Zone (e.g., us-west1, eu-central1)
- Live GPU pool (count, by SKU)
- GPU-equivalent capacity (A100-80GB-eq) computed as sum(count * sku_factor)
- Effective tokens/sec capacity estimate (tokens/sec per A100-eq * eq_count)
- Target tokens/sec (P50/P90) and percent headroom
- Spare-equivalent requirement (units) = max(floor(runway_shortfall/A100_equip_tokens), ceil(spare_multiplier * expected_failure_rate * live_count))
- Tranche plan: immediate (0–6m), near-term (6–18m), optional long-term (18–30m) with SKU recommendations
- CAPEX band estimate (USD) per tranche (list of per-unit costs used: H100=54k, A100=40k, L40s=35k, RTX-6000=12k)

Zone-level example table (text-form sheet):
Headers: Zone | Live A100-eq | Tokens/sec/A100-eq | Effective tokens/sec | P90 target | Headroom (%) | Spare-eq target | Immediate tranche | Near-term tranche | LT optional | CAPEX immediate | Notes
Row (us-west1 example):
us-west1 | 28.4 | 45k | 1,278,000 | 2,000,000 | -36.1% | 8 | +8 H100 (immediate) | +12 A100 (6–18m) | +6 L40s (18–30m) | $432,000 | heavy chat load, recommend H100 for long-context latency

Explanation of formulas (human readable):
- Live A100-eq = sum(sku_count * sku_factor)
- Effective tokens/sec = Live A100-eq * tokens_per_A100_eq (tokens_per_A100_eq derived from perf bench for model family; editable)
- Headroom (%) = (Effective tokens/sec - P90 target)/P90 target * 100
- Spare-eq target = ceil(max( (P90 target - Effective tokens/sec)/tokens_per_A100_eq, rotation_spares, floor(failure_rate*live_count*spare_rotation_months/12) ))
- Tranche sizing rules: immediate tranche should cover spare-eq target + 20% capacity buffer if headroom negative; near-term tranche can be mixed SKUs to buy on market timing and cost advantage; long-term tranche is optional and for strategic SKU diversification.

Hedging matrix (conceptual):
Columns: Procurement confidence | SKU preference | Typical use case | % allocation of tranche
- High confidence (short lead time) | H100 | long-context / latency critical | 60% immediate, 40% near-term
- Medium confidence | A100 | steady throughput | 30% immediate, 50% near-term
- Opportunistic | L40s / RTX fallback | burst/offload batch | 10% immediate, 10% near-term, 100% long-term optional

Sensitivity scenarios (built-in switches):
1) Demand spike x1.5 for 3 months (simulate P90 up to 3.0M tokens/sec) — outputs additional urgent tranche and estimated on-prem borrowing months.
2) 20% SKU price increase — recompute CAPEX bands and show effect on preferred mix.
3) 30% slower procurement (lead-time +30 days) — increases spare-eq target and shifts immediate tranche.
4) Quantization rollout success reduces tokens/sec per A100-eq requirement by 18% — recalc headroom and reduce near-term tranche.
5) Cross-zone failover activated (50% of peak rerouted to neighbor) — shows net delta across zones and suggests inter-zone spare pool.

Spare rotation and sustainment rules (short bullets):
- Maintain at least 1.1x spare-eq for zones with P90 headroom < 0.
- Rotate 20% of spares into production every 6 months to avoid warranty cliff / obsolescence clustering.
- Keep an emergency stash of 2 units of heterogeneous small-footprint GPUs (RTX-6000 equivalents) in each region for emergency routing while long-lead SKUs ship.

Quick decision heuristics for procurement reviews:
- If headroom <= -25% and lead time > 10 weeks -> approve expedited immediate tranche (H100 preferred).
- If price delta (H100 vs A100) > 25% and demand P50 < 75% of P90 -> favor A100 in near-term tranche.
- If quantization program threshold met (quality metric delta < 3%) -> reduce near-term tranche by 15%.

Notes, open questions and action items (todo list):
- [ ] Validate tokens/sec per A100-eq benchmarks for new redwood/chat family (enqueue a perf run with 4 long-context prompts). Assigned: Miguel. Due: 2026-12-01.
- [ ] Confirm procurement discounts with partner X (target: 8–12% off list) — Samir to follow up, add to CAPEX table. Due: 2026-12-08.
- [ ] Add support for mixed-precision cost model (fp16 vs int8) in the sheet so we can simulate quantization improvements. Assigned: Riley. Due: 2027-01-10.

Appendix A — Example tranche calculation (walkthrough):
Given us-west1 baseline above: P90 gap = 722k tokens/sec -> tokens_per_A100_eq=45k -> shortfall eq = ceil(722k / 45k) = 16 eq units. Spare-rotation rule min(6 months) => expected failures ~0.03/year*28.4 ~= 0.85 -> rotation buffer => 2 eq. Immediate tranche = shortfall + rotation buffer -> 18 eq. Translate to SKUs: prefer H100 for 60% -> 11 H100 units, remainder fill with A100. CAPEX immediate = 11*54k + 7*40k = $594k + $280k = $874k (sheet rounds to nearest 10k).

Appendix B — Short glossary of terms used in the sheet:
- A100-eq: normalizing factor for capacity counting across SKU types.
- Spare-eq: spare-equivalent unit measured in A100-eq.
- Runway (months): months until we exhaust spares under stress scenario assuming given failure rate and demand profile.

Changelog (for this doc):
- 2026-11-12 A.Kapoor initial draft with hedging matrix and sample zone row.
- 2026-12-15 added sensitivity toggles and tranche cost model.
- 2027-01-20 updated SKU factors after bench run v3 and adjusted spare rules.

Conversation links / refs:
- Slack: #private-deploy-capacity (thread: "hedging-matrix-procurement")
- Confluence: private-vpc-install-guide (linked for ops playbooks)

Free-form notes (notes-to-self style):
- Could we model holding cost as % of CAPEX per month and add an NPV tradeoff for earlier vs later purchases? (probably yes — nice to add to the LT tranche logic)
- Think about a zone-level emergency swap contract with cloud partner for 3-month coverage at fixed cost (cheap insurance).

End of workbook summary: this file should be used in planning reviews to pick tranche allocations per zone, compute immediate spare needs, and run the five sensitivity toggles during weekly capacity sync. Keep it lean: run the perf bench and update tokens_per_A100_eq whenever model mix changes.
